doc: Strands Agents: its own name for the system prompt, and the parts its semconv-latest telemetry writes for blocks the conventions have no part type for.

carriers.doc: The system prompt a model was given, reported beside the conversation: a detached request frame.

detect.doc: The **weak** evidence, and its rank is the whole point: the SideSeat SDK defaults service.name to `strands-agents`, so this rule's service-name signal would otherwise claim every span of every framework using the SDK. The phrase search covers the three spellings a name may use and was a Rust matcher. The producer's own self-identification is a separate alternative at its own rank, because one rank for signals of different strength has to be placed for the weakest of them.
detect.label: StrandsAgents

alternatives.doc: The producer naming **itself**, which is the strongest evidence there is - and at rank 280 it sat behind `openinference.`, so a Strands span carrying any OpenInference attribute was labelled OpenInference. Placed immediately before that rule and nowhere earlier: moving the whole rule up would have taken the defaulted service name with it, and every other relative order is deliberately unchanged.

observed_in.doc: The census shows 1.55.1 stopped writing system_prompt; every capture before it carries it, 1.57.2 does not.

messages.doc: The instruction the agent was given, read as a message. Ranked ahead of every conversation carrier because it frames the request rather than answering it - the retired code emitted it first for the same reason. Blank counts as absent: the attribute is written whether or not there is a prompt.

observed_in.doc: Every default-profile capture carries the bundled result beside the reply; under semconv-latest the result arrives as its own tool message instead.

messages.doc: A choice event may carry a bundled tool result beside the model's reply, in the provider's own envelope. Reported as its own observation - and *added* to the event's raw form rather than replacing it, because the reply is wanted too. Tagged as a tool result rather than a tool message, so history filtering does not remove it; the bundle is split at query time, which is what keeps a fix applying to stored data.

attach.doc: The first identified call in the bundle, which identifies the message; the rest are recovered when it is split.

content_blocks.doc: Strands 1.12's semconv-latest telemetry writes a whole Bedrock content list as one part: `{"type": "text", "content": [{"text": ...}, {"toolUse": ...}]}`, whatever the blocks are. Each member is a block in the message's place - the prompt's text, the calls, the results handed back - so the list is spliced in and each is read as the provider block it is. A text part whose content is a string is the conventions' own and is not touched.

Strands' semconv-latest telemetry writes a Bedrock content block the conventions have no part for as a part typed with the block's own key, its value under `content`: reasoning arrives as `{"type": "reasoningContent", "content": {"reasoningText": {...}}}`. Nothing read that, so the model's reasoning rendered as an unknown block holding raw JSON. A redacted block carries no text and keeps its opaque payload out of the text.

Strands 1.12's semconv-latest tool span writes a call's arguments as a one-member list holding them under `content`, `[{"content": {"city": "Paris"}}]`, where later releases write the object itself. Read through the list, or the tool span's copy of the call disagreed with the model's and both survived.

tool_use.name: $.name
tool_use.doc: The JavaScript SDK's flat form of a Converse tool call: the members beside a camelCase type tag.

tool_result.doc: Its tool result. A failure is stated as a status rather than a flag.
